chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: A Commodore-issued date with Ella Fitzgerald
summary: The listing names Eddie Stanfield on bass and Ella on vocals; McRae never heard the record and notes that Commodore issued many such sides.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: True chart and then Eddie Stanfield -- that was the bass player. Then Cozy, and Ella was on the vocals.
I didn't know him too well.
See, this date was put together --
This is another date. Now when you played this date for me, I never have heard this date.
See, because a lot of these records they came out -- Commodore used to put them out. They always come out, you know, through Commodore Records. And they put out all these jazz things.
Unless you went into Commodore, you wouldn't get them at the regular stores, you know.
Yeah. It seems that Brunswick -- they were actually recording --
See, we never knew who they were recorded
